title: Four Reasons to Add Beans to Your Diet
paragraphs: Beans come in lots of tasty varieties — like kidney beans, soybeans, broad beans and pinto beans for example — and are among the healthiest foods you can eat. Here are four reasons to add them to your meals.

Beans have a lot of good things in them. They're an excellent source of fiber. Half a cup of black beans will give you about a quarter of your daily fiber requirement. They are also full of important vitamins and minerals like folic acid, iron and Vitamin B6. And, they are an excellent source of plant-based protein.
The fiber in beans is great for your gut health. On a very basic level, fiber supports digestion and regular bowel movements, but it also supports a healthy gut microbiome.

The gut microbiome is all the different bacteria, viruses and other organisms found in our intestines. A healthy microbiome helps with things like digestion and fighting disease by controlling potentially harmful organisms.

Better gut health also means a reduced risk of colorectal cancer, but that's not the only way that beans can help prevent cancer. All that fiber makes beans very filling and satisfying, helping prevent overeating and obesity.
That's important because obesity has been linked with 13 different types of cancer, including breast cancer, stomach cancer and meningioma, a type of brain cancer.

Including beans in your diet could help prevent heart disease too. One study found that eating a serving of beans once a day over six weeks led to a significant drop in the levels of participants' LDL cholesterol, or "bad cholesterol." High LDL cholesterol is linked to an increased risk of having a heart attack or stroke.
Another study found that regularly eating beans was associated with lower blood pressure. And high blood pressure is also heavily associated with heart attacks and strokes.
